{
  "research_question": "Do mouse navigation performance metrics (Time-to-Target, Success, Path Efficiency, Average Speed, and Angular Dispersion) differ significantly across five stimulation paradigms: Combined, ICMS Only, Dim Visual Only, Bright Visual Only, and Sham?",
  "stim_paradigms_compared": ["Combined", "ICMS Only", "Dim Visual Only", "Bright Visual Only", "Sham"],
  "response_variables": ["Time-to-Target", "Success", "Path Efficiency", "Average Speed", "AD"],
  "anova_plan": [
    "For Time-to-Target: One-way ANOVA with Stim Paradigm as the fixed factor. Given the severe right skew (max=201.39 vs mean=2.81, sd=2.08), consider log-transformation or Welch's ANOVA to handle heteroscedasticity. The bounded minimum of 0.5 suggests a shifted distribution.",
    "For Success: Binary outcome (0/1) makes ANOVA inappropriate. Use logistic regression with Stim Paradigm as categorical predictor, or chi-squared test of independence, or Cochran-Armitage trend test if ordering hypothesized. Binomial GLM with logit link is preferred for formal inference.",
    "For Path Efficiency: One-way ANOVA with caution. Extreme right skew (max=29.82 vs mean=0.47, sd=0.47) and bounded [0,1]-ish range suggest beta regression or transformation. Values >1 indicate path redundancy; consider Winsorization or robust ANOVA.",
    "For Average Speed: One-way ANOVA. Moderate right skew (max=75.35 vs mean=12.50, sd=4.46) suggests checking homogeneity of variance. Welch's ANOVA may be needed if variance differs across paradigms.",
    "For AD (Angular Dispersion): One-way ANOVA. Bounded [0,1] with mean=0.38, sd=0.24. Right-censored at 1.0 (n at max unknown). Beta regression or arcsin-sqrt transformation preferred given natural bounds."
  ],
  "assumptions_and_diagnostics": [
    "Independence: Verify no temporal autocorrelation within mice; the 8 mice contribute repeated measures. Current plan treats observations as independent, which is violated. Mixed-effects models with Mouse as random effect more appropriate.",
    "Normality: Shapiro-Wilk or Anderson-Darling tests on residuals; Q-Q plots. For Time-to-Target, Path Efficiency, and Average Speed, log-transformation likely needed.",
    "Homoscedasticity: Levene's and Bartlett's tests. Large sample sizes (n=76655) make tests sensitive; examine variance ratios. Welch's ANOVA as fallback.",
    "Sample size imbalance: Combined (48846) vs Bright Visual Only (3323) creates 15:1 ratio. Type I error inflation minimal, but power and confidence interval width vary.",
    "Outliers: Examine influence metrics (Cook's distance, leverage). Time-to-Target max=201.39 and Path Efficiency max=29.82 are extreme but possibly valid long-duration trials."
  ],
  "posthoc_plan": [
    "If omnibus test significant (or meaningful effect size): Pairwise comparisons with Tukey HSD for ANOVA models, controlling family-wise error rate across 10 pairwise tests.",
    "For Welch's ANOVA: Games-Howell post-hoc test appropriate for unequal variances and sample sizes.",
    "For logistic regression (Success): Estimated marginal means with Tukey-adjusted pairwise odds ratios, or sequence of orthogonal contrasts focusing on Combined vs Sham and Combined vs single-modality conditions.",
    "For beta regression (Path Efficiency, AD): Estimated marginal means on response scale with Tukey adjustment.",
    "Effect sizes: Cohen's d for continuous variables (with Hedge's g correction for unequal n), odds ratios for Success, and pseudo-R² for GLMs."
  ],
  "expected_findings": [
    "Combined stimulation (n=48846, dominant condition) likely shows fastest Time-to-Target, highest Success rate, and optimal Path Efficiency compared to single-modality or Sham, based on typical multisensory enhancement literature.",
    "ICMS Only (n=11378) expected to outperform Sham and possibly visual-only conditions on speed metrics, given direct cortical activation.",
    "Dim Visual Only vs Bright Visual Only: Potential U-shaped or asymmetric effects; dim vision may impair more than bright if near detection threshold, or bright may cause distraction.",
    "Sham (n=3505) expected baseline performance, though small sample limits precision.",
    "High variability in Path Efficiency (sd=0.47 with mean=0.47, max=29.82) suggests substantial heterogeneity in navigation strategies, potentially washing out paradigm effects.",
    "AD mean=0.38 suggests relatively directed paths; paradigm effects may be subtle given restricted range and ceiling at 1.0."
  ],
  "limitations": [
    "Severe imbalances in sample sizes across paradigms (Combined 48846 vs Bright Visual Only 3323) reduce precision for small-group comparisons and complicate variance interpretation.",
    "No accounting for repeated measures structure: 8 mice with ~9500-11000 trials each violates independence assumption. Linear mixed models with Mouse as random intercept essential for valid inference.",
    "Success as binary outcome analyzed via ANOVA would be invalid; logistic framework required.",
    "Path Efficiency values >1 and AD values at exactly 1.0 indicate boundary violations for standard parametric models.",
    "Temperature=1.0 for LLM generation may affect reproducibility; confirm this analysis is deterministic.",
    "Summary-only data view precludes examination of trial-level temporal structure, learning effects, or session blocking that may confound paradigm comparisons."
  ],
  "recommended_next_analysis": "Fit linear mixed-effects models for Time-to-Target, Path Efficiency, Average Speed, and AD with Stim Paradigm as fixed effect and Mouse as random intercept; use generalized linear mixed model with binomial family for Success. Include session/block covariates if available. Contrast Combined against each single-modality and Sham with Dunnett's method. Report marginal means with 95% confidence intervals and cluster-robust standard errors to account for mouse-level correlation."
}
